text: Wizard: Universalist

Out of all wizards, those most studious and dedicated to
understanding the Art are called universalists. The path many
accomplished archmages chose to walk even as young
practitioners, universalists have no care for perfection of a
single school of magic or casting style, since they believe in
the one True Magic. In pursuing it, they attain incredible
mastery of the arcane, being able to reshape magic in ways
even their colleagues find extraordinary.

To be a universalist, however, is not only about producing
grandiose displays of magical crafting. Universalists, in their
core, understand the Weave, the mana, and some say are
those closest to peering through the veil of magic itself. While
all wizards seek revelations hidden behind the arcane
mystery, universalists see magic as the means of perfecting
themselves and the world around them.
Arcana Savant
2nd-level Universalist feature

Enamored by the beauty of knowledge, you have delved
further into the intricate secrets of magic. You gain
proficiency in the Arcana skill. If you are already proficient in
the Arcana skill, you double your proficiency bonus for any
ability check that uses that skill.

In addition, the time you must spend to copy any wizard
spell into your spellbook is halved.
MASTERS OF ARCANA
Advanced Learning
2nd-level Universalist feature

Your advanced pace of learning brings forward knowledge
untouched by other practitioners of the art. When you gain
this feature, choose one spell from any class. A spell you
choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown in the
Wizard Table.

You add the chosen spell to your spellbook, and it counts as
a wizard spell for you.

You add one additional spell from any class to your
spellbook at 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, 11th, 13th and 17th level.
Modify Magic
6th-level Universalist feature

Your extensive study over the arcane arts allows you to
modify spells. When you add or copy a wizard spell in your
spellbook, you can choose to modify the spell's formula that
you write in your spellbook in the following ways:

Alter Energy. If the original spell deals acid, cold, fire,
lightning or thunder damage, you can replace damage
type with one other type from that list. If the original spell
deals multiple damage type from that list, the new damage
type replaces all types from the original spell.
Alter Manifestation. If the original spell requires saving
throws, you can change the saving throws from one ability
score to another of your choice.

A spell modified by this feature counts as a different spell
from the original and therefore counts against the number of
wizard spells you can prepare. For example, a 1st-level
wizard universalist that has a scroll containing the 1-st level
spell burning hands and wishes to copy the spell to their
spellbook can choose to modify the copied spell to deal cold
instead of fire damage. If the wizard later decides to also copy
the original burning hands spell to their spellbook, they can
choose to prepare burning hands, the modified spell, or both
when preparing their wizard spells.
Rapid Preparation
10-th level Universalist feature

Your studies have taught you the importance of preparation.
As a bonus action, you can replace one spell you have
prepared with another spell from your spellbook.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your
Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once) . You regain all
expended uses of this feature when you finish a long rest.
High Arcanum
14th-level Universalist feature

Unearthing the deepest parts of the wizard's craft, you gain
access to High Arcana. When you finish a long rest, you can
choose to gain one of the following benefits:

Arcane Fire. When you deal damage to a creature with a
spell, you can expend a spell slot to deal extra force
damage to that creature. The extra damage is equal to
2d10 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d10 for each spell
level higher than 1st.
Arcane Reach. When you cast a spell that has a range of
5 feet or greater, you can expend a spell slot to increase
the range of the spell by 60 feet per level of the spell slot.

Archmage's Sight. You have truesight out to a range of
120 feet.
Sage's Knowledge. If your total for an Intelligence check
is less than your Intelligence score, you can use that score
in place of the total.
Spell Power. The spell save DC for your wizard spells
increases by 1.

The chosen benefit lasts until you finish a long rest. You
expend a 5-th level or higher spell slot to change the chosen
benefit to another one.
